Sample dynamic additive effects with AR(1) evolution

Source: R/RcppExports.R
sample_dynamic_ab_cpp.Rd

Gibbs update of the per-period additive effects under the AR(1) state model with stationary initial condition. For each actor and period the full conditional combines the AR(1) bridge prior (stationary init at t = 1) with the dyadic residual likelihood: resid_ij = a_i + b_j + e_ij.

Usage

sample_dynamic_ab_cpp(
  a_current,
  b_current,
  Z_array,
  EZ_array,
  rho_ab,
  sigma_ab,
  s2,
  symmetric,
  rho_dyad = 0,
  center = FALSE,
  rvar = TRUE,
  cvar = TRUE
)

Arguments

a_current

Current 2D array of row effects (n x T)

b_current

Current 2D array of column effects (n x T)

Z_array

3D array of latent positions (n x n x T)

EZ_array

3D array of expected values without additive effects (n x n x T)

rho_ab

AR(1) parameter for additive effects

sigma_ab

Innovation standard deviation

s2

Dyadic residual variance

symmetric

Whether the network is symmetric

rho_dyad

Within-dyad correlation of the residual pair (e_ij, e_ji); 0 (the default) treats the dyads as independent. Ignored for symmetric networks and for non-square slices. Must lie strictly between -1 and 1 for a directed square panel.

center

Whether each period's effects are drawn conditional on summing to zero across the actors of their margin, the identification used when the model has a static intercept. The draw is then the conditional of the block's joint normal given the constraint, not a projection of an unconstrained draw.

rvar

Whether the sender margin is active.

cvar

Whether the receiver margin is active.

Value

List with updated a and b arrays

Details

With rho_dyad = 0 the dyads are independent, e_ij ~ N(0, s2), and the conditional for a_i uses only row i of the residual. With rho_dyad != 0 the two directed residuals of a dyad are jointly normal, (e_ij, e_ji) ~ N(0, s2 * ((1, rho), (rho, 1))), whose inverse covariance is ((q, p), (p, q)) with q = 1 / (s2 (1 - rho^2)) and p = -rho / (s2 (1 - rho^2)). The effect being drawn enters e_ij directly and enters the pair's cross term through e_ji, so each fully observed dyad contributes q to the precision and q (r_ij - b_j) + p (r_ji - a_j - b_i) to the numerator of the a-step (symmetrically for the b-step). A dyad with only one direction observed falls back to the marginal isotropic weight 1 / s2.

The reciprocal effect (b_j for the a-step, the freshly updated a_i for the b-step) is subtracted from each residual, missing residuals are skipped, the diagonal is skipped, and for symmetric networks each dyad contributes exactly once (resid(i,j) = a_i + a_j + e_ij) so the pair term does not apply and rho_dyad is ignored.
